use_case_name: Clear Exercise Surveillance Data on an Exercise Status Order

evidence_cards.content: The reporting of IFF/SIF surveillance data in the J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words for Air and Surface tracks is the responsibility of the JU with R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the high-level objective (goal) for the primary actor (JU with R²), which is to report surveillance data.

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to resolve differences in the Environment/Category, ID, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, Exercise Indicator and Special Interest Indicator field values using the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section explicitly defines the objective of the 'Change Data Order' process, which corresponds to the use case of clearing exercise surveillance data on an order.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message is used to rapidly clear the Exercise Indicator and all artificial data from exercise tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective of the use case: clearing the Exercise Indicator and artificial data upon receipt of the specific order message.

evidence_cards.content: The use case 'Clear Exercise Surveillance Data on an Exercise Status Order' aims to clear exercise surveillance data as part of the J7.0 Track Management (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This directly defines the goal of the use case: clearing exercise surveillance data via a specific track management action.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message is transmitted by the JU with R² to indicate that the JU with R² specified in the Source TN field has dropped or has ceased reporting the track specified in the Reference TN field.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the core objective of the use case: transmitting a drop track report to indicate cessation of tracking for a specific reference, which aligns with clearing exercise surveillance data upon status order.

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to clear Exercise Surveillance Data on an Exercise Status Order.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message is used to rapidly clear the Exercise Indicator and all artificial data from exercise tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states the high-level objective of the use case: clearing exercise indicators and artificial data upon receipt of an Exercise Status Order.

evidence_cards.content: For any track with Exercise Indicator set to value 1, Exercise Track, data concerning the track must be considered artificial, for exercise purposes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state (Exercise Indicator = 1) that marks a track as 'artificial', which is the condition required before the use case can begin to clear such data.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 2) message is mandatory for reception and the data must be displayed to the operator.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system state regarding message reception that applies generally to the environment where Exercise Status Orders operate.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific precondition state (possession of R² and lack of implementation) that alters standard processing behavior.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message is used to rapidly clear the Exercise Indicator and all artificial data from exercise tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the purpose of the message which implies the precondition that this message exists and is intended for clearing exercise data.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall take the following actions on all tracks in their database which have the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the system state required for the use case to execute: there must be tracks in the database with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.

evidence_cards.content: The interface must be able to return to a 'No Data' status for the specified track and its corresponding mode(s) when erroneous codes are detected and no other valid codes are available or changes are inhibited.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a necessary system capability (returning to No Data status) that must exist before the use case of clearing data can successfully complete; it implies the system must be in a state where this transition is possible.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU capable of originating a J3 message that includes a continuation word containing IFF/SIF data shall also have a capability to manually originate the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a mandatory precondition capability for the actor (JU): if it handles certain IFF/SIF data, it must possess the specific ability to generate the clearing message (J7.5 ACT=0) required for the operation.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.5 (ACT = 0) CLEAR IFF/SIF message is transmitted by any JU to initiate clearing of IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific message and actor action that constitutes the main flow step for clearing surveillance data in this use case context.

evidence_cards.content: Clearing IFF/SIF data via J7.5 (ACT = 0) is initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that the triggering mechanism for the clear operation is manual operator initiation, which constrains how the main flow begins.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific action (assuming R²) triggered by a J7.0 message receipt, which is part of the interaction sequence for this use case.

evidence_cards.content: Immediately prior to assuming R² for an air or surface track after receipt of a Drop Track message, a JU shall test the track for correlation in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a conditional step (correlation test) within the flow following a Drop Track message.

evidence_cards.content: The page contains no evidence for the main_flow of clearing Exercise Surveillance Data using a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: The document text exclusively details rules and procedures for the J7.0 (ACT = 2) Change Data Order message, which is explicitly excluded from the scope of the current use case.

evidence_cards.content: The provided page contains no information regarding the J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message or the clearing of Exercise Surveillance Data.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall automatically set the Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first specific action in the main flow sequence triggered by the Exercise Status Order.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall automatically set all data fields that may contain artificial information to the No Statement, default value, or actual values if held in database, and set the Exercise Indicator to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This step fulfills the core goal of clearing artificial data and resetting the exercise indicator.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall break any locally originated engagement involving the TN by transmitting a J10.2 (WES = 8) message to report the engagement broken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a mandatory system response within the normal success scenario for the order.

evidence_cards.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, all JUs shall terminate any locally originated Command message with Command values 2, 3, 5, or 7 involving the TN, by transmitting a J9.0 message with the Command field set to value 4 (Cease Engage), or value 5 (Hold Fire), if the Engagement Status field is set to value 4 (Firing).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific termination logic required for active commands as part of the exercise status order flow.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may originate, by operator action only, the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message for the clearing of one or more modes on the specified track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the initiation step in the main flow: the C2 JU (as a JU) performs an operator action to send the J7.5 (ACT=0) clear message.

evidence_cards.content: All JUs, upon receipt of the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, shall automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status (except that acceptance or rejection of a received J7.5 (ACT=0) Mode IV Clear message may be automatic or by operator determination).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system’s automatic response to the clear message — setting modes to No Data status — which is the core success behavior in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The operator display shall indicate that a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message was received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a required user interface feedback step in the main flow after message receipt, confirming successful processing to the operator.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message is a valid Information Management data type used for the exchange of surveillance data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific message code and action required to execute the main flow of clearing exercise surveillance data.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a): if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a legal alternative path for automatic correlation during exercise data clearing when conflicting IDs exist between tracks, diverging from standard OCC restrictions — directly relevant to alternative_flow.

evidence_cards.content: In this exception, the Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2), allowing breaking of engagement and/or destroying missile(s) in flight.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the outcome of the alternative flow: which track is dropped and what operational effect it enables — critical for defining the variant’s success boundary.

evidence_cards.content: This exception shall not be applied by any JU upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message; thus, any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a constraint that terminates the alternative flow under specific conditions — essential for bounding the scope of the alternative path and identifying when it must not proceed.

evidence_cards.content: An alternative path for clearing IFF/SIF data exists where the J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message is transmitted by any JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific message and actor capability for clearing surveillance data that diverges from the main flow of using a J7.0 Exercise Status Order.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of the J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message is initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the trigger mechanism (operator action) for this alternative flow, distinguishing it from automated system responses or status orders.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU receives a Surveillance message or a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message in which the air, surface (maritime), or land (ground) Environment/Category and ID are different from the local Environment/Category and ID, the Environment/Category conflict shall be processed and resolved prior to the resolution of the ID conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where a conflict detection mechanism triggers a specific processing sequence (resolving Environment/Category before ID) instead of the standard data update path.

evidence_cards.content: If an Environment/Category conflict is detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict need occur.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the success boundary for this alternative flow variant: once the primary conflict is resolved, the secondary check is skipped.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message to resolve differences, it shall reject any received data on that track that differs for a 30-second lock-out period.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the system handles incoming exercise data by discarding it rather than processing it normally, following the clearing order.

evidence_cards.content: After receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, no messages with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1 shall be originated until local operator action is taken to reenable the JU to accept and originate exercise tracks.

evidence_cards.content: When rejecting the correlation due to holding OCCs or conflicting IDs upon receipt of a J7.2 message, the JU acts in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).

evidence_cards.content: If for any reason, such as operator error, it is desired to change the simulation status of a track, the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, and a new track shall be reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling path for changing simulation status: dropping the track and reporting a new one instead of modifying the existing track.

evidence_cards.content: The one exception to this rule is that a change from live to simulated shall be accepted if the track is being received from an FJU.

evidence_cards.content: For NonR² JUs, if an ID conflict is indicated and the unit follows Table 4.7-2 actions, it shall inhibit transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 1) until the surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0.

evidence_cards.content: If the R² JU identifies that an ID conflict exists, the operator shall be alerted, local ID data continues to be reported with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1, and the conflict will be resolved by manual means.

evidence_cards.content: Exception to the 30-second lock-out rule: JUs shall accept different data prior to the completion of the lockout period provided the different data is from the same source that originated the previous J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
